{{Short description|Nigerian academic and university administrator}}
'''Adekunle Olusola Adeyeye''' (born 1 May 1968)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nigerian physicists famous people|url=https://famous-scientist.com/nigerian-physicists-famous-people/|date=31 March 2020|website=Famous Scientists|access-date=29 May 2020}}</ref> is a Nigerian [[Academy|academic]] and university administrator,<ref name=the>{{cite news|title=From Nigeria to Cambridge to Singapore|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/hub/national-university-singapore/p/nigeria-cambridge-singapore|work=Times Higher Education|access-date=24 July 2019}}</ref> announced in July 2019 as principal of [[Trevelyan College]], [[Durham University]].<ref name=newheadstweet />

== Biography ==
Originally from Nigeria, Adeyeye received his first degree from the [[University of Ilorin]], in [[Kwara State]], Nigeria, before moving to the [[UK]] to study for a master's degree in microelectronics engineering at the [[University of Cambridge]], followed by a PhD in physics at the university's [[Cavendish Laboratory]] in 1996.<ref name=techreview /><ref name=researchgroup>{{cite web|url=https://www.adeyeye-group.com/people|title=Adeyeye Research Group - People|publisher=National University of Singapore|access-date=24 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190724125047/https://www.adeyeye-group.com/people|archive-date=24 July 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1996, he was the first Nigerian elected as a research fellow at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], but left in 1997 to take up a 9-month post as a senior research engineer at the Data Storage Institute, a research and development organisation established by the [[National University of Singapore]], before returning to Trinity College.{{Citation needed|date=May 2020}} In 2000, he was a founding researcher at the Information Storage Materials Laboratory at the National University of Singapore, becoming a full professor in 2012.<ref name='the' /> In 2014, he became the first head of [[National University of Singapore#Ridge View Residential College|Ridge View Residential College]], the University of Singapore's first residential college outside University Town.<ref name='straits'>{{cite news|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/nus-to-set-up-first-residential-college-outside-of-utown|title=NUS to set up first residential college outside of UTown|work=The Straits Times|date=13 March 2014|access-date=25 July 2019}}</ref>

In 2002 he was cited by ''[[Technology Review]]'' as one of their 100 innovators under 35 "whose work and ideas will change the world".<ref name='techreview'>{{cite news|url=http://www2.technologyreview.com/tr35/profile.aspx?TRID=225|date=1 June 2002|title=Innovators under 35: Adekunle Adeyeye|work=Technology Review|publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology|access-date=24 July 2019|archive-date=10 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181110143734/http://www2.technologyreview.com/tr35/profile.aspx?trid=225|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] and the [[Institute of Nanotechnology]], and was an [[IEEE Magnetics Society]] Distinguished Lecturer in 2013.<ref name=researchgroup /> In 2018, Adeyeye was elected to fellowship of the [[American Physical Society]] "[f]or contributions to synthesis and characterization of magnetic nanostructures and their applications in low power magnonic information processing."<ref>{{cite news |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm |publisher=American Physical Society}}</ref>

Since January 2020 he has been [[Principal (academia)|Principal]] of [[Trevelyan College, Durham|Trevelyan College]], Durham, and Professor of Physics at [[Durham University]].<ref name=newheadstweet>{{cite tweet|user=durham_uni|author=Durham University|number=1147151911281483778|title=We are delighted to announce the appointment of five new Heads of College who will join us in 2019/20.|date=5 July 2019}}</ref><ref name=newhead>{{cite web|url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/experience/colleges/newheadsofcollege/adekunleadeyeye/|title=Professor Adekunle Adeyeye - Principal of Trevelyan College and Professor of Physics|website=Durham University|access-date=24 July 2019}}</ref>

He is married to Adefolake and has a daughter and two sons.<ref name='the' />

== Bullying controversy ==
In August 2021 [[The Guardian]] newspaper published an investigation into Adeyeye's alleged bullying and harassment of staff. He was accused of bullying, misogyny and frequently reducing his staff to tears. It was reported that within 16 months, two members of staff had filed formal grievances against Adeyeye and three resigned amid concerns over his behaviour. After being approached by The Guardian newspaper, Adeyeye stepped down from Durham University's bullying policy committee.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Halliday |first1=Josh |title=Durham University keeps college head in post despite alleged intimidating conduct |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2021/aug/01/durham-university-keeps-trevelyan-college-head-adekunle-adeyeyein-alleged-intimidating-conduct |access-date=15 August 2021 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=1 August 2021}}</ref>

The Durham branch of the [[University and College Union]] released a statement saying the case highlighted "extremely important structural issues" at the university,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Halliday |first1=Josh |title=Durham University failing on bullying, staff say |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2021/aug/05/durham-university-failing-on-bullying-former-staff-say|access-date=28 September 2021 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=5 August 2021}}</ref> alongside tweets stating "If the behaviour is found to be as alleged, we regard it as shocking and cannot accept it as a union",<ref>{{cite news |last1=UCU|first1=Durham|title=Durham UCU Statement |url=https://twitter.com/ucuatdurham/status/1423203230838894598|access-date=29 September 2021 |work=[[Durham UCU]] |date=5 August 2021}}</ref> while [[Durham Students' Union]] expressed solidarity with staff and students at the college, saying "a lack of specific action risks normalising unacceptable behaviours".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Twins|first1=Seun|title=Seun Twins: Statement on Bullying and Harassment |url=https://www.durhamsu.com/articles/seun-twins-statement-on-bullying-and-harassment|access-date=28 September 2021 |work=[[Durham Student Union]] |date=5 August 2021}}</ref> University newspaper [[Palatinate (newspaper)|Palatinate]] reported that over 20 alumni had pledged to withhold donations from Durham University while Adeyeye remains in post. <ref>{{cite news |last1=Burman|first1=Theo|last2 = McHardy|first2 = Martha|title=Durham alumni withhold donations after Trevelyan Principal intimidating behaviour allegations |url=https://www.palatinate.org.uk/durham-alumni-withhold-donations-after-trevelyan-principal-intimidating-behaviour-allegations/|access-date=28 September 2021 |work=[[Palatinate (newspaper)|Palatinate]] |date=4 August 2021}}</ref>

In September 2021, staff and students, including student leaders representing almost 8,000 members of the Durham University student body, signed an open letter accusing Durham University of apathy towards bullying in response to Adeyeye's alleged conduct.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Halliday |first1=Josh |title=Students and staff at Durham University complain of 'apathy' over bullying |url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2021/aug/05/durham-university-failing-on-bullying-former-staff-say|access-date=28 September 2021 |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=28 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Students and staff at Durham University complain of 'apathy' over bullying |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-tyne-58717598|access-date=28 September 2021 |work=[[BBC News]] |date=28 September 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Hundreds of Durham University students and alumni 'no longer trust leaders' amid bullying complaints |url=https://www.itv.com/news/tyne-tees/2021-09-28/durham-university-students-no-longer-trust-leaders-amid-bullying-complaints|access-date=28 September 2021 |work=[[ITV News]] |date=28 September 2021}}</ref>
